stock.counterargument: It is an expensive stock: 70.6× trailing earnings and a 4.5% free cash flow yield, so the growth is already in the price and one weak quarter would cost a lot.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +35.5%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $83.26 on the decision date.
risks: The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-10-29, 22 days before the decision date.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-11-20.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2026-02-04) plus 364 days

stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
stock.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.title: Kenya and DR Congo agree to restore ties after tensions over conflict
stories.excerpt: The two leaders committed to upholding sovereignty and "non-interference in the internal affairs of states".
stories.lead:
Kenya's President William Ruto and his Congolese counterpart Felix Tshisekedi have agreed to restore full diplomatic ties between the two countries following tensions over the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

Relations between the two countries have soured since 2023 when DR Congo accused Kenya of hosting leaders launching a rebel alliance, including the M23.

This led DR Congo to recall its envoy to Nairobi. Relations deteriorated further when Kinshasa refusing to accredit Kenya's nominated ambassador.

stories.title: Burnham to tell MPs 'landmark' EU deal could make next decade 'much better'
stories.excerpt: The prime minister will tell MPs the deal agreed on Friday is a "choice between a broken status quo or change".
stories.lead:
The prime minister will tell Parliament on Monday the "landmark" deal struck with the EU means there is a "very real prospect" the next decade can be "much better" than the last one.

The deal, which covers British food exports, emissions trading and a youth experience scheme, is a "choice between a broken status quo or change", Andy Burnham will tell MPs.

He will also call it "the single biggest growth measure to be delivered in this parliament" - repeating his claim it could add £17bn to the British economy.

stories.title: Do not feed the animals. Vets explain why hats, coins and shoes can be deadly.
stories.excerpt: It's not easy to retrieve foreign objects from animals once ingested. Some things can be grabbed using an endoscope. But if an item gets far into the intestinal tract, surgery isn't always possible.
stories.lead:
The death of Fiona, a beloved hippopotamus who captured hearts, has renewed calls to remind zoo visitors that animals can die from swallowing foreign objects.

Fiona, 9 years old, died Thursday after ingesting a hat that accidentally ended up in her habitat at the Cincinnati Zoo. The zoo said that the hat was lodged in the hippo's small intestine and surgery was not possible.

"Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible, but her body couldn't fight anymore," Cincinnati Zoo Director Dave Jenike said in a statement.

stories.title: Poundland is facing collapse - what's gone wrong?
stories.excerpt: Poundland has a matter of days to find a buyer or face collapsing into administration. Why?
stories.lead:
People have not stopped shopping at Poundland - quite the opposite.

Although the chain was struggling when it was sold by Pepco last year for £1, the business turned a corner over the year to September, going from a £68m loss to an £18.1m profit before interest, tax and certain accounting charges.

Going into the vital Christmas period, first-quarter like-for-like sales were up 7% and operational profits of £1.9m were up £1.2m on last year.

stories.title: Pip assessments need 'fundamental overhaul', report to say
stories.excerpt: Disability Minister Sir Stephen Timms says he will recommend major reforms to the personal independence payment.
stories.lead:
A review into the personal independence payment (Pip) will call for a "fundamental overhaul" of the assessment process to "better recognise people's varying costs and needs", the disability minister has said.

Sir Stephen Timms has been looking into disability benefits in England and Wales for the past year and found the set up was "no longer fit for purpose".

Writing in the Times, external, he said his review, to be published on Tuesday, would recommend people with the most severe conditions have a "fast track" process which is "less burdensome".

stories.title: Water Polo Champions Again!
stories.excerpt: Fordham water polo wins sixth straight MAWPC title.
stories.lead:
Lewisburg, Pa. – All gaming fans knew that the League of Legends World Championships were held last weekend at Barclays Center. All gaming fans also know that the South Korea's T1 team holds the record with six World Championships, most recently winning in 2025. Though playing a much different game, the Fordham water polo team, ranked fifth in the nation, matched T1's title record, winning its sixth straight MAWPC championship today with a 24-15 win over #16 Navy at Bucknell's Kinney Natatorium.

With the win, Fordham improves to 25-3 on the season and receives the conference's automatic bid to the NCAA Championship to be held from December 4-6 at Canyonview Pool in La Jolla, California.
